model: SE8600 Series Rooftop Unit, Heat Pump and IAQ Controller (2015 BACnet list)
equipment_type: Rooftop unit controller (room thermostat, conventional or heat-pump RTUs)
applies_to: Schneider Electric SE8600 Series touchscreen room controllers for conventional rooftop units and heat pumps with economizer and indoor air quality (CO2 / fresh air) control.
summary: The SE8600 is an SE8000 Series touchscreen room controller for rooftop units and heat pumps (MV 119 Application), with staged G/Y1/Y2/W1/W2 outputs, economizer and CO2 / fresh-air control. It is a BACnet application-specific controller on BACnet MS/TP and also carries a weekly occupancy schedule and calendar, ten Lua program objects and status for up to ten ZigBee wireless zones. This is the April 2015 object list; names differ from the later Viconics VT8650 / SpaceLogic guides.
notes: Access follows the manual's property tables: AV, AO, BV, BO and MV present values are commandable, CSVs are writable, and AI, BI and MSI (MI here) inputs are read-only (AI and MSI only writable while Out_Of_Service is TRUE).

Lua Program 1-10 are BACnet Program objects (typed Other here); the Lua script is held in each object's Description property. Occupancy Schedule (SCH 1) holds 7 days with 3 occupied / 3 unoccupied times; Occupancy Calendar (CAL 1) holds dates, ranges and weekends.
Wireless Zone 1-10 objects (AI IEEE address, MV set function, MI status / battery / paired) only report data for ZigBee sensors paired to the controller.
Names are as printed, including spellings such as 'Dehumidifcation Lockout'. Ranges and defaults from the range tables are given in the descriptions.

source.title: SE8600 Series BACnet Integration Manual - Rooftop Unit and Indoor Air Quality Controller

integration.summary: Set a MAC address from 0 to 127 (the factory value 254 keeps BACnet off), then command occupancy (MV 10), system mode (MV 16), fan mode (MV 17) and the occupied setpoints (AV 39 / AV 40). Read room temperature (AV 100), effective occupancy (MI 33), the G/Y/W stage outputs and the alarm BVs. Use priorities 4-16 for live commands.

minimum_points.name: Occupancy Command
minimum_points.why: BMS occupancy: local, occupied or unoccupied

integration.enable: BACnet communication starts once the MAC address is changed from the factory value 254 to 0-127. The BMS then writes MV 10 Occupancy Command (1 = Local Occupancy, 2 = Occupied, 3 = Unoccupied) and MV 16 System Mode. MV 110 Occupancy Source picks motion or the internal schedule for local occupancy.
integration.heartbeat: No heartbeat point. If the controller goes offline, network-bound Room Temperature, Outdoor Temperature and Occupancy are released.
integration.remote_sensors: The manual lists Outdoor Temperature (AV 101) as a global value the BMS can send to all controllers and Room Temperature (AV 100) for testing and override. Writes at priority 4-16 override the controller's own value until relinquished or power is lost.
setup: Factory MAC address is 254, which disables BACnet; set 0-127 to join the token ring.
Default Device ID is 86000 + MAC (MAC 63 gives 86063); the device name and ID are writable.
Up to 64 Schneider Electric nodes per segment and 128 per network; 510 ohm bias resistors, at most two sets per segment.
gotchas: Priorities 1-3 are saved to flash and survive a power cycle, locking the value until a NULL is written at the same priority; use 4-16 (RAM) for live control and rewrite after a restart.
CSV 1 / CSV 2 screen messages are not saved and are lost on power loss.
Remove configuration objects from the BAS after setup to cut polling traffic, as the manual recommends.
MV 119 Application switches between rooftop and heat-pump sequences; MV 117 sets the reversing valve as O or B.
